stableFrontendBehaviors: Library detail pages may mount LibraryAccessWidget to render backend-derived access context for a chosen library.
Admin consumers may use /admin/subscriptions and /admin/subscriptions/{libraryId} as the first stable subscription inspection entrypoints.
Frontend code may re-read and re-render access context, admin subscription state, and history after bounded payment-event mutations.
Mock billing interactions are stable only as thin consumers of POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/{libraryId}/events and must not own lifecycle transitions locally.
downstreamHandoffRule: Replay, provider realism, checkout, webhook, and correction flows must open a follow-up lane instead of widening S0F-9D in place.
Downstream frontend work may compose the current panels and pages, but must continue treating backend responses as the source of truth for plan_code, subscription_state, and entitlements.
No downstream UI code may mutate subscription_state directly or bypass ApplyPaymentEventUseCase through ad hoc client-side state machines.
If a later lane needs live UI-visible lifecycle proof, it should record browser/runtime evidence against the existing endpoints and entrypoints rather than redesigning the first consumer loop.
localUiVerificationRecommendation: Start the local backend and frontend stack.
Open /admin/subscriptions, select a real library UUID, and verify access-context plus admin state render successfully.
Emit upgrade_success and renewal_failed from the mock billing panel and confirm the admin state/history panels re-read backend truth.
Record the first live UI-visible lifecycle chain in a follow-up evidence artifact if the lane needs to be marked stable.
